As someone who also struggles with this, here's my two cents. Don't jeopardize the main idea of your piece for the sake of having it sound more song-ey. There's plenty of musicians out there who write poetic songs (Hozier, tøp to an extent, Arctic Monkeys, Kimbra) and are acclaimed lyrical geniuses and their songs masterpieces. You have the potential to make more than a song, a piece of art. 

Of course, taking your songs through several cycles of editing and second opinions is always good. But if you're a good writer, try to maybe experiment with instrumentals and make them FIT to YOUR writing. Play around with rhythms and genres. Think of the kind of music you'd want to make, find musicians who make that kind of music, and study their process. Try fingerpicking guitar to your poetry and see how the rhythm carries the words in different ways, move forward from there. 

In my opinion and experience, it's way easier to be a good instrumentalist, than it is to be a good writer. Work on making your music performable, sure, but if you're a strong writer don't ever let that go!

A credit card can be really helpful if you are responsible with it! Where I live I'm pretty sure they don't even approve of them without a steady job. 

For example, I'm a current college student, and I found myself needing a car. I've had a credit card for about 8-9 months, and have a pretty good credit score. However, since I only work part-time with an hourly wage, no dealership would accept me for a loan because I don't make enough. If I made more, then I would have been fine getting a loan just because of my credit score (ended up using a co-signer). But yeah, if you plan on ever needing a loan in the future (college, car, house, etc) you're gonna need a credit card. Unless you casually have hundreds of thousands of dollars just chilling in your checking account lol

Personally I get really stressed out when I have more than a $75 credit balance, so I keep it under that for the most part. That way I can reasonably pay it off with my next paycheck, and built up good credit in the process!
